newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFFER still to consider Nat. Grid views.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFFER still to consider Nat. Grid views.

text.p: UK electricity watchdog OFFER head Stephen Littlechild wants to see if there is anything "different or more persuasive" in submissions on price controls made by National Grid Group Plc, he told Reuters.
"I want to see if the National Grid Company has anything different or more persuasive to say than they had last time," he said, speaking on the fringes of Britain's annual science festival here.
National Grid had earlier described Littlechild's price control proposals as "totally unacceptable" and "based on ill-founded assumptions."
Littlechild said he had not yet had a chance to consider National Grid's submission which is in response to OFFER's fourth consultation document released earlier this year.
OFFER's plans include an effective revenue reduction of 22-28 percent for National Grid in 1997-98 and subsequent annual reductions in prices of RPI minus 4.0 points.

"It's going to take a little while to assess further evidence so i think it's premature to say what chances were of a particular outcome," Littlechild said, adding that he still expected to make proposals by the end of September.
OFFER will also be considering submissions from other groups as well as the National Grid before finalising its decision on price controls.
